speaker: Doctor
text: Please tell me, how old were you when you first noticed swelling in your knee, and does the pain improve with rest? Also, do you or any family members have a history of gout, hemophilia, or early-onset arthritis?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease (idiopathic avascular necrosis of the femoral head).

I am suspicious of this condition given the age (walking age), monoarticular knee swelling (referred pain from the hip), lack of trauma, and family history. Please have the child lie on their side so I can perform a flexion and abduction test of the hip, and I will request an X-Ray of the right hip to visualize the femoral head.
